brief.video_title: ChatGPT for Data Analysis Build Charts in 5 Minutes vs. 5 Hours - Lillian Chiu
brief.viewer_outcome: Viewers will be able to execute a 4-step AI workflow using ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude to analyze raw data, build strategic learning agendas, and generate presentation-ready charts.
brief.target_audience: Data analysts, business analysts, and professionals who regularly create data-driven presentations.
brief.delivery_tone: casual, informative, and highly practical (vlog-style tutorial)
core_talking_points: The Modern AI Data Workflow vs. The Old Way
Step 1: Build a Learning Agenda with ChatGPT
Step 2: Build Initial Charts with Gemini
Step 3: Refine Chart Storytelling with Claude
Bonus: Upgrading Creative Assets with Freepik
Step 4: Apply Human Judgement to the Data
brief.selected_angle: Treating different AI models as specialized agents in a multi-step analytical workflow, rather than relying on a single tool to do everything.
misconceptions: One single AI tool can perfectly handle the entire data analysis pipeline.
AI charts are ready to present right out of the box without human refinement.
must_avoid: Deep-dive technical SQL or Python coding tutorials.
Skipping the planning (learning agenda) phase of analysis.

outline.section_title: The Modern AI Data Workflow vs. The Old Way
outline.purpose: Introduce the value proposition of AI fluency and contrast the manual data pipeline with the optimized multi-tool AI pipeline.
outline.entry_assumption: The viewer believes data visualization requires hours of manual formatting in Excel/Google Sheets.
outline.exit_state: The viewer understands that AI fluency means knowing exactly which tool to use for specific analytical steps.
outline.misconception_to_preempt: AI completely replaces the analyst in one click.
talking_points: Real AI fluency is about knowing when and where to effectively use AI to yield the best results.
The old workflow was pulling SQL, visualizing manually in Sheets, and building slides manually.
The new workflow optimizes specific steps using ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.
evidence_needed: Visuals of the old manual workflow vs. the new streamlined AI workflow.
Logos of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude.

outline.section_title: Step 1: Build a Learning Agenda with ChatGPT
outline.purpose: Show viewers how to structurally plan their analysis before touching any visualization tools.
outline.entry_assumption: The viewer thinks they should immediately start making charts from raw data.
outline.exit_state: The viewer will use ChatGPT to generate a structured 'Learning Agenda' to guide their analysis.
talking_points: Task: Analyze Duolingo's 2025 user growth using public SEC data.
Step 1 is to build a learning agenda, acting as a Google Doc outline for your analysis.
Use ChatGPT to generate questions that guide what you actually need to visualize.
evidence_needed: Screen recording of the generated Learning Agenda in Google Docs.

outline.section_title: Step 2: Build Initial Charts with Gemini
outline.purpose: Demonstrate how to quickly generate baseline charts directly within the Google Sheets environment.
outline.entry_assumption: The viewer builds charts by manually highlighting rows and clicking 'Insert Chart'.
outline.exit_state: The viewer will use Google Gemini's side-panel integration to auto-generate baseline charts from prompts.
outline.misconception_to_preempt: AI charts look perfect on the first try.
talking_points: Import data into Google Sheets.
Paste the prompt from the learning agenda into the Gemini side panel.
Gemini provides a fast first draft, but it usually lacks good business storytelling.
evidence_needed: Screen recording of Gemini in Google Sheets generating a basic chart.

outline.section_title: Step 3: Refine Chart Storytelling with Claude
outline.purpose: Teach the viewer how to use Claude to upgrade basic charts into presentation-ready, annotated visuals.
outline.entry_assumption: The viewer manually adds text boxes and arrows to charts in PowerPoint.
outline.exit_state: The viewer will use a 'Master Chart Design Prompt' in Claude to automatically generate annotated, beautifully formatted charts.
outline.misconception_to_preempt: Claude is only for text generation.
talking_points: Provide Claude with a master chart design prompt, raw data, the agenda question, and the base Gemini chart screenshot.
Request two versions: a clean version and an annotated version with insights.
Use the annotated version as a visual guide to quickly polish your final presentation.
evidence_needed: Detailed view of the 'Chart Refinement Template for Claude'.
Before and after comparison of the Gemini chart vs. the Claude chart.

outline.section_title: Bonus: Upgrading Creative Assets with Freepik
outline.purpose: Show an adjacent AI workflow for sourcing and generating creative assets (icons, video upscaling) for presentations.
outline.entry_assumption: The viewer searches Google Images for random, mismatched icons.
outline.exit_state: The viewer will use Freepik's AI suite to generate cohesive icons and upscale assets in one place.
talking_points: Freepik is an all-in-one creative AI suite.
Use the AI assistant to brainstorm visual concepts.
Use AI upscalers to fix blurry footage and generate matching icon sets instantly.
evidence_needed: Screen recording of Freepik's UI, upscaler tool, and icon generation.

outline.section_title: Step 4: Apply Human Judgement to the Data
outline.purpose: Reinforce the necessity of the human analyst in reviewing AI outputs for business logic and nuance.
outline.entry_assumption: The AI's final chart can be copied and pasted directly to the CEO.
outline.exit_state: The viewer will manually adjust AI phrasing and verify data implications before presenting.
outline.misconception_to_preempt: AI insights are flawless and perfectly understand business context.
talking_points: Regardless of the tools used, always apply human judgement at the end.
Adjust phrasing (e.g., changing 'Q4 Pending' to just 'Pending').
Break down the data from different angles to ensure the true business driver (e.g., APAC region, retention vs. new users) is accurately represented.
evidence_needed: Screen recording showing specific textual edits being made to the final Claude output.

outline.purpose: Wrap up the tutorial, provide a community call-to-action, and transition into a personal lifestyle vlog segment.
outline.entry_assumption: The video ends immediately after the technical tutorial.
outline.exit_state: The viewer feels a personal connection to the creator and is encouraged for the new year.
talking_points: Finding the right AI tool mix is key to the modern workflow.
You overestimate what you can do in a day, but underestimate what you can do in a year.
Holiday vlog: Saks 5th Ave window displays, NYC street food, and decorating a Christmas tree with a puppy.
evidence_needed: Vlog footage of NYC, shopping, eating, and a dog.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Step 1: Build a Learning Agenda with ChatGPT.
visual_direction: Tan graphic title card.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Before I do any analysis, I always start with a learning agenda.
visual_direction: Speaker in bright kitchen setting.
storyboard.action_notes: 1:27 - Hard cut back to speaker.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Think of it like a Google Doc outline with key questions that guide your analysis, so you don't get lost in the data and you keep your analysis structured. We're answering these questions, starting with: How are monthly active users per quarter trending over time? I always ask myself the 'so what', like the business rationale behind pulling this data. I used this prompt in ChatGPT, and you can find the step-by-step in this video which a lot of you have found helpful. And it has a Gemini prompt so we can visualize later.
visual_direction: Screen recording of Google Doc taking up mostly left/center, speaker video overlay floating on the right side.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Step 2: Build Charts with Gemini.
visual_direction: Tan graphic title card.
storyboard.action_notes: 1:59 - Hard cut to full screen title card reading 'Step 2: Build Charts with Gemini'.

storyboard.voiceover_text: I've already imported the data into Google Sheet. Then I click Gemini from the side panel and paste the Gemini prompt from the learning agenda. So, 'visualize monthly active users by quarter for 2023, 2024, and 2025.' Gemini gives me a first draft. But, it's missing storytelling. It's hard to understand what the insight is. And previously, I would just manually adjust the chart. But now, I'm going to use Claude to help me enhance the chart's storytelling.
visual_direction: Screen recording of Google Sheets. Speaker PiP on bottom left.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Step 3: Chart Storytelling with Claude.
visual_direction: Tan graphic title card.
storyboard.action_notes: 2:26 - Cut to slide showing 'Before' chart. 2:28 - Cut to slide showing 'Final' annotated chart. 2:29 - Hard cut to full screen title card reading 'Step 3: Chart Storytelling with Claude'.

storyboard.voiceover_text: First, I have this master chart design prompt that teaches Claude what to do. All the rules I've built over the years of doing business analysis on how to make your graphs strategic and easy to understand. These are also the fundamentals I teach in my Business Analytics course. You can find everything in the link below. In the chart design prompt, I have rules like: use callout boxes to highlight key insights in the graph, make sure colors have visual hierarchy, focus on the main point. If we're benchmarking, use at least two previous years to justify.
visual_direction: Screen recording of a Markdown document with prompt rules. Speaker PiP on left.
storyboard.action_notes: 2:32 - Hard cut to screen recording of document with speaker PiP. Scrolling through rules like Visual Hierarchy, Brand Colors, etc. 2:43 - Cut to a quick montage of course materials. 2:48 - Cut back to the Markdown document screen recording, scrolling through rules.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Then I give Claude this prompt. I attach the master chart design prompt, I state what I'm working on, what the goal is, what brand it is so it can use that brand palette. I always attach the raw data for accuracy. I paste the entire learning agenda question so it knows how to think about the insights. I attach the Gemini chart screenshot. Then I ask it to give me two graphs. Version 1 is a clean, ready-to-paste graph into my presentation. Version 2 is an annotated graph with all the storytelling as a visual guide. I will just use version 2 as a visual guide to polish version 1 much faster. So now you can see Claude is telling me 2025 growth is decelerating. We're growing at 19% year-over-year so far versus 32% and 45% in previous years.
visual_direction: Screen recording of Claude interface. Speaker PiP on left.

storyboard.voiceover_text: With AI, now you can even use AI in your creative process. Like Freepik, which has quickly become one of the creative tools I reach for the most.
visual_direction: Speaker in bright living room setting.
storyboard.action_notes: 3:50 - Hard cut to speaker full screen. 3:52 - Split screen graphic with a robot icon and 'FREEPIK' logo pops up.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Freepik is an all-in-one creative AI suite. Meaning instead of jumping between 5 different apps, Freepik puts AI tools and a huge professional asset library all in one place. Let's say when I'm planning videos and I'm stuck on how to visualize concepts, I can use Freepik's AI assistant to brainstorm ideas. Like different ways to visualize graphics, concepts, or even aesthetic directions for a topic. And to elevate my video footages, I can also use Freepik's upscale and retouch tools to clean everything up. It sharpens the footage and fixes little imperfections automatically. It's like giving my camera a tiny upgrade without actually buying one. And yes, Freepik still has all the icons and templates that you can easily find and use. For instance, for the AI Agent video, I needed a robot icon to represent the AI tools I've been talking about, and I found the perfect one in seconds. So no more digging through the internet for random mismatching graphics. Everything just looks cohesive. So if you're a creator and you want a single place where you can generate visuals, fix footages, design graphics, and pull from this massive library of professional assets, Freepik honestly makes the whole process so much faster. You can discover Freepik's free AI tools with the link in the description.

storyboard.voiceover_text: Regardless of what AI tools I use, I always apply human judgement at the end. I changed 'Q4 Pending' from just 'Pending' so it's more clear we're only in Q3 right now. If I were to do this analysis, I would break down the user growth from two more angles. From a regional level, you can see APAC is the growth driver. EMEA is a growth detractor. That's something we can note to the local teams. Growth is retention-led. So sustaining retaining users while paying attention to new users that's declining.
